changes.summary: Era restriction on contact-fusion material: the GOAT script's material filter gathers from LOCATION_MZONE while the modern one gathers from LOCATION_ONFIELD, so under the modern implementation an 'X-Head Cannon' or 'Y-Dragon Head' sitting in the Spell/Trap Zone as a Union equip can be banished as material, and under the historical one only monsters in the Monster Zone qualify (upstream annotation: 'Only mo[n]sters in the mzone allowed as material'). The printed material clause never distinguishes the zones - it says 'the above cards on your side of the field', later 'the above cards you control' - so this is a period ruling; chronology unresolved.

changes.summary: Functional erratum: 'This card cannot be Special Summoned except by removing from play the above cards' became 'Must first be Special Summoned (from your Extra Deck) by banishing the above cards you control ... Cannot be Special Summoned from the Graveyard', i.e. a strict nomi became a semi-nomi with a Graveyard ban. The GOAT script passes `true` as Fusion.AddContactProc's summon-condition argument, which (per proc_fusion.lua) creates an EFFECT_SPSUMMON_CONDITION with no value and so forbids every other Special Summon of the card; the modern script passes a function allowing any Special Summon except from the Extra Deck or Graveyard, so once properly contact-fused the modern card can later be Special Summoned from banishment. The same printing reworded the discard effect into PSCT targeting wording, which the script diff shows is not a targeting change.

review.notes: Baseline text is v1 (DR1-EN106, Dark Revelation Volume 1, 2005-03-19, matched at 0.9985 - the residue is line-break handling), which is also the printing in force at the 2005-04-01 GOAT snapshot. v0 (MFC-051, 2003-10-10) says 'the above monsters' and predates the baseline. Lineage v2 and v3 carry no card number, no set and no date in the packet, so they cannot be dated by set-release evidence; both keep the strict 'This card can only be Special Summoned ... by removing from play the above cards' form (v2 adds the redundant 'cannot be Special Summoned from the Graveyard' line, v3 renames Fusion Deck to Extra Deck), so they are behaviourally identical to v1 and are recorded here rather than as an unresolved-chronology change that would needlessly block period snapshots. The erratum entry therefore collapses v1 -> v4. The two remaining script-diff hunks (`REASON_COST|REASON_MATERIAL` and `REASON_COST|REASON_DISCARD` versus the '+' forms) are equivalent. The Monster-Zone material ruling and the 2016 erratum cannot be sequenced against each other because the former has no chronology.
